description:
## CONTEXT

The keystone reliability item from the 2026-07-03 lens design review (decision record: workspace N-076; codex cross-model rulings 1-10; oracle field report). On a live review a true-positive major finding nearly died because a lens reported a `line` that disagreed with the finding's real location and the consumer anchor gate rejected it; only manual realignment saved it. Root cause: findings anchor on a bare `(file, line)` pair with no quoted source evidence, so a one-line drift is unrecoverable and is silently dropped downstream. This ticket moves the producer from self-reported `(file, line)` trust to text-verified anchoring: the server already receives the artifact at hop-1 and can verify a quoted line against it at hop-2 with zero repo access. Binds codex ruling 4 (anchor repair-or-flag lives IN the main result, never metadata-only counts) and the owner floor+edge ruling (harden the static floor).

## VERIFIED STATE @ a9f49dd

- The finding shape has no evidence/quote field. `findingObjectShape` (src/schema/finding.ts:21-30) is `id, severity, category, file, line, description, suggestion, confidence`. Both `LensFindingSchema` (finding.ts:57-61) and `MergedFindingSchema` (finding.ts:76-92) are built from that one shared shape (finding.ts:16-20 documents "add or rename a field here exactly once"), so a field added there propagates to both.
- The finding-format section of the shared preamble (src/lenses/prompts/shared-preamble.ts:105-127) lists exactly those fields in its JSON example and never states the coordinate system for `line`. Line 125 constrains `line` to "a positive integer or JSON null" but does not say new-file vs old-file vs hunk-relative. The artifact is labeled `Diff:` for CODE_REVIEW (shared-preamble.ts:176-179) while the Read tool shows post-change files (shared-preamble.ts:149-155), so a lens can legitimately emit any of three coordinate systems.
- The token `evidence` is on the V1 denylist (test/lens-bodies.test.ts:97-106, enforced at 168-181). That test only scans each lens BODY via `lens.render(stage)`; the finding-format JSON example lives in the shared preamble, which the denylist test does not cover. The new field must nonetheless be named `snippet` (not `evidence`) so no lens body ever needs the banned token.
- `ReviewSession` (src/state/review-state.ts:52-67) retains `prompts`, `promptHashes`, `perLensExpiresAt`, `cachedResults` but NOT the artifact or changedFiles (a grep for `artifact`/`changedFiles` over src/state and the on-disk index at src/cache/in-flight.ts:99-129 returns nothing). `registerReview` (review-state.ts:176-220) and its callsite (src/tools/start.ts:234-246) never pass them.
- `lens_review_complete` (src/tools/complete.ts:284-476) merges outputs but never verifies any finding location against source text. Dedup drops non-ok lenses (src/merger/dedup.ts:43) and keys on `(file, line, category)` (dedup.ts:50), so a drifted line breaks dedup silently.
- The recovery-window pattern this fix mirrors lives in the consumer verifier (workspace repo), which is out of scope here; the fix belongs at the producer.

## SCOPE

1. Add a `snippet` object to `findingObjectShape` (finding.ts:21-30): `{ quote: string (min 1, max ~400 chars, the exact source line(s) at `line`), startLine: positive int }`. It rides the shared shape so `LensFinding` and `MergedFinding` both gain it. Keep `LensFindingSchema` `.strict()`. The field is schema-OPTIONAL (a missing snippet must never reject the whole payload -- back-compat + graceful degradation, owner ruling) but is declared MANDATORY in the preamble contract and enforced-for-anchoring at complete-time by severity (steps 3-4).
2. Retain artifact + changedFiles: add `artifact: string` and `changedFiles: readonly string[]` to `ReviewSession` (review-state.ts:52-67); thread through `registerReview` params (review-state.ts:176-220) and the callsite (start.ts:234-246); persist into the in-flight index (`IndexRecordSchema`, in-flight.ts:99-129) so a restart can still verify. Size-cap the persisted artifact at `MAX_FILE_BYTES` (in-flight.ts:59).
3. Verify at complete. In complete.ts (after per-lens parse, within/before the merger), for every finding carrying a `snippet`: locate `snippet.quote` in the retained artifact -- for CODE_REVIEW against the diff's NEW-side (post-change) lines only, for PLAN_REVIEW against the plan text -- within a +/-N line recovery window (N default 10, configurable). On a match at a line different from `finding.line`, overwrite `finding.line` (and `snippet.startLine`) from the matched location and record both original and matched line on the emitted finding (add `anchorRealignedFrom: number | null`).
4. Unverifiable handling by severity. A finding whose `snippet` fails to verify (or is absent) routes to `deferred[]` with a NEW `DeferralReason` value `evidence_unverified` (schema/review-protocol.ts) -- EXCEPT blocking/major findings, which SURVIVE in the main `findings[]` with `line: null` plus a `reviewIntegrity` warning entry in the verdict envelope naming the finding id and reason. Add first-class verdict counts `anchorRealignedCount` and `evidenceUnverifiedCount` -- never metadata-only, never silent (codex ruling 4).
5. Preamble contract. Add to the finding-format section (shared-preamble.ts:105-127): (a) one sentence -- "`line` is the 1-based line number in the post-change (new) version of `file`, as shown by Read; never use diff-hunk-relative or old-file numbering."; (b) the `snippet` field in the JSON example with -- "quote the exact source line at `line` verbatim into `snippet.quote` and set `snippet.startLine` equal to `line`."

## OUT OF SCOPE

Repo-access execution verification (stays in byte-review); adjudication fields (LF4); the consumer-side verifier changes (workspace); dedup-on-evidence-span (LF3 builds on this); cache re-validation (LF7 builds on this); the delta transport (LF6 builds on this retention). This ticket lands producer-side anchoring + artifact retention + the preamble contract only.

## ACCEPTANCE

- Unit test: a finding whose `snippet.quote` matches a line 3 below its reported `line` is realigned; the emitted finding has the corrected `line` and records the original in `anchorRealignedFrom`.
- A blocking-severity finding with a non-matching `snippet` is NOT dropped: it appears in `findings[]` with `line: null` and a `reviewIntegrity` entry naming its id.
- A minor finding with a non-matching or absent `snippet` appears in `deferred[]` with reason `evidence_unverified`, and `evidenceUnverifiedCount` reflects it.
- Realignment and unverifiable counts are present on the verdict envelope and equal the number of findings in each bucket, enforced by a `superRefine` mirroring the existing count invariants (schema/verdict.ts:86-96).
- Restart test (mirror T-024 via `_clearMapOnlyForTests`, review-state.ts:595-597): after a memory-only clear, a complete call still verifies snippets because the artifact rehydrates from the in-flight index.
- Pinned preamble test in test/shared-preamble.test.ts asserts the new line-semantics sentence and the `snippet` field appear verbatim.
- The V1 denylist test (test/lens-bodies.test.ts) still passes -- no lens body contains `evidence`; the new field is `snippet` and lives in the preamble.

## PITFALLS

- Do NOT name the field `evidence` (test/lens-bodies.test.ts:104 denylist).
- Do NOT hard-reject payloads missing `snippet` at the schema boundary -- that breaks back-compat and graceful degradation; enforce presence at complete-time by severity instead.
- The diff artifact contains both old (`-`) and new (`+`) lines; verify quotes against NEW-side content only, else a deleted line matches spuriously.
- Preserve the existing `hadAnyFindings` / severity-count superRefine invariants (schema/verdict.ts:86-190) when adding new count fields; every new count needs its own consistency check or a future regression goes undetected.
- Keep `MergedFindingSchema` and `LensFindingSchema` in lockstep by editing only `findingObjectShape` (finding.ts:16-20).

## VERIFICATION

Build a two-lens fixture review: lens A reports a finding at the correct line with a matching snippet; lens B reports the same defect one line off with a matching snippet. Run start -> complete; assert the emitted finding is realigned and both lenses appear in `contributingLenses`. Then flip lens B's snippet to a non-matching string and assert it is deferred (minor) or integrity-flagged (blocking) with the corresponding count field set. Diff the rendered preamble against the pinned snapshot.

## SIZING

L. Touches schema/finding.ts, schema/verdict.ts, schema/review-protocol.ts (DeferralReason), state/review-state.ts, cache/in-flight.ts, tools/start.ts, tools/complete.ts, lenses/prompts/shared-preamble.ts, and the merger. Cross-cutting but each change is mechanical; the risk is in the verification-window semantics. Portable enough for the lowest permitted execution tier if the recovery-window algorithm is specified precisely in the plan.

Cross-link: workspace N-076. Keystone -- LF6 (retention enabler), LF7 (cache re-validation), and LF3 (evidence-span dedup) build on it.

## PLAN-REVIEW RULINGS (2026-07-04, wave 3b, binding):

Adjudicated from the wave-3a plan gate: plan v1 round 1 (codex verdict revise, 4 findings; adversarial reviewer verdict approve, 6 advisories) and plan v2 round 2 (adversarial verdict revise: 1 blocker, 2 majors, 1 advisory, 1 minor). Every disputed fact re-verified in this repo at HEAD 770cfd5 (T-030 landed; suite 599/599). Plan v2's internal design rulings 1-8 are RATIFIED as amended below. The next planner MUST fold R1-R13 in from the start; reviewers and byte-review MUST treat them as spec.

R1 (resolves round-2 BLOCKER: PLAN_REVIEW cross-domain mis-realignment). Anchor verification, realignment, deferral, and integrity-flagging are CODE_REVIEW-ONLY. In PLAN_REVIEW the anchor pass always runs in normalize-only mode (the same mode as the missing-artifact case): strip lens-supplied `anchorRealignedFrom`, never realign, never defer, never flag, contribute 0 to both counts. Derivation: `fileLineCorrelation` (src/schema/finding.ts:37-48 at 770cfd5) forces every localized finding (`line !== null`) to carry a non-null `file`, and in PLAN_REVIEW that file is a repo source path the server cannot verify from plan text (the retained artifact is the plan document; no plan-document file convention exists). The set of legitimately verifiable plan-stage findings is therefore empty, and matching source-file quotes against plan-text coordinates can actively corrupt correct anchors (plans embed fenced code blocks). This SUPERSEDES the SCOPE 3 phrase "for PLAN_REVIEW against the plan text". Mandated test: a PLAN_REVIEW finding with `file: "src/x.ts", line: 42` and a snippet whose quote also appears in the plan text at a different line within the window is NOT realigned, NOT deferred, NOT flagged, and keeps line 42. Consequence for fixtures: every test exercising realignment/deferral/flagging MUST run stage CODE_REVIEW with a diff artifact whose new-side contains the quoted lines; existing PLAN_REVIEW-driven complete tests remain pass-through. The preamble snippet mandate (SCOPE 5) stays stage-neutral: plan-stage snippets are accepted and carried but not server-verified (the consumer-side verifier may use them later).

R2 (resolves round-2 MAJOR: out-of-diff CODE_REVIEW findings silently degraded). In CODE_REVIEW, enforcement applies ONLY to findings whose `file` has an entry in the diff-derived new-side line index (exact path match, as the plan documents). A localized finding whose file is ABSENT from that index (unchanged file, deleted file, binary file) PASSES THROUGH: no realignment, no deferral, no line-nulling, no reviewIntegrity entry; only server-owned fields are stripped. Rationale: the server retains only the diff and has nothing to verify against; ruling 4's "absence of server evidence must never brick a review" applies per-file. The motivating incident (wrong line in a CHANGED file) stays fully enforced: a finding on an in-index file whose quote finds no match within the window takes the standard defer/flag path -- including quotes of unchanged lines outside hunk context in a changed file, which is intentional and mirrors the downstream consumer anchor gate. The `changedFiles` start param is NOT the enforcement key; the parsed diff new-side index is. Mandated tests: (a) a blocking finding on an out-of-index file with a correct verbatim quote survives in `findings[]` with its line intact and no integrity entry; (b) a minor finding likewise is not deferred; (c) an in-index no-match still defers/flags.

R3 (resolves round-2 MAJOR: total-loss path for source lines over 400 chars). Keep the SnippetSchema quote cap at 400. The preamble instruction (SCOPE 5b) must add: if the source line exceeds 400 characters, quote exactly its first 400 characters. Matcher rule: candidate artifact line L matches quote Q iff `Q === L`, or `Q === L.trim()`, or (`L.length > 400` and (`Q === L.slice(0, 400)` or `Q === L.trim().slice(0, 400)`)). This closes both failure arms verified at HEAD: a >400-char verbatim quote fails LensFindingSchema `.strict()` at hop-2 and the finding-phase parse failure replaces the ENTIRE lens payload with the `status: "error"` placeholder (src/tools/complete.ts:358-387, placeholder at 371-383), permanently losing all of that lens's findings across retries; a naive client-side truncation could never satisfy full-line equality. Mandated test: an artifact containing a >400-char line plus a finding quoting its 400-char prefix verifies (and realigns when off by a few lines).

R4 (resolves round-2 ADVISORY on deviation sign-off; also round-1 codex MINOR on count semantics). Both deviations are RATIFIED here as binding spec; byte-review must not flag them. (a) `anchorRealignedCount` is PRE-dedup operational telemetry (`AnchorPassResult.realignedCount`): the number of input findings the server realigned this round. The verdict superRefine enforces only the sound direction, `anchorRealignedCount >= |emitted findings and deferrals carrying anchorRealignedFrom|` (strict inequality is legal via dedup loss; the field is server-minted, so emitted can never exceed the operational count). ACCEPTANCE bullet 4 is AMENDED accordingly: exact-equality superRefine applies to `evidenceUnverifiedCount` only (integrity entries and evidence_unverified deferrals are never deduped, so equality is sound there). Mandated test: a realigned finding that loses the dedup confidence-winner selection still increments `anchorRealignedCount`. (b) `snippet` and `anchorRealignedFrom` are `.optional()` (absent means no snippet / not realigned), NOT `.nullable().default(null)`: tsconfig strict + exactOptionalPropertyTypes makes defaulted fields required in z.infer output and would force edits across every finding literal in ~9 test files; wire semantics are identical (consumers read `f.anchorRealignedFrom ?? null`). SCOPE 1's and SCOPE 3's literal signatures are amended to match.

R5 (resolves round-2 MINOR: round-2 test blocks bypass the helper). The plan must name every inline `handleLensReviewStart` call in test/tools-complete.test.ts that hardcodes the artifact literal "## Plan\n\nDo the thing." and keep those literals byte-identical to whatever round-1 artifact the extended `startPlanReview` helper produces for that test, or round-2 promptHashes diverge and the `cached[]` assertions fail. At 770cfd5 the inline calls sit at lines 463, 1026, 1091, 1150, 1217, 1327, 1377, 1428 (locate by content, not line number). Any test whose round-2 start must hit the prompt cache changes in lockstep with its round-1 artifact.

R6 (resolves round-1 codex MAJOR: confidence-floor vs survive+flag contradiction; also the approve-round orphaned-integrity-entry advisory). Ratified plan ruling 5: survivorship precedence is `alwaysBlock > confidenceFloor > evidence-survival`, enforced INSIDE the anchor pass. An unverified localized finding takes the survive+flag path iff `alwaysBlockSet.has(category) OR (severity in {blocking, major} AND confidence >= confidenceFloor)`; every other unverified localized finding defers with reason `evidence_unverified` (which therefore covers unverified minors/suggestions AND unverified blocking/major below the floor without an alwaysBlock category -- document this on the DeferralReason enum). blocking-policy.ts (floor comparison at src/merger/blocking-policy.ts:62) needs NO changes, and the invariant holds that `applyBlockingPolicy` can never floor-defer an integrity-flagged finding's dedup representative, so reviewIntegrity entries always reference findings present in `findings[]`. Do NOT bypass the floor for flagged findings: a garbage or absent snippet must never become a survival strategy. All `evidence_unverified` deferrals preserve the claimed `line`; only the survive+flag path nulls it. Mandated tests: low-confidence unverified blocking and major findings (no alwaysBlock category) land in `deferred[]` as `evidence_unverified`; fixtures asserting survive+flag MUST use confidence >= floor (the helper default 0.8 vs floor 0.6 already satisfies this).

R7 (resolves round-1 codex MAJOR: character cap vs byte read gate). Ratified plan ruling 6: the persisted artifact is capped by ENCODED BYTES of the serialized IndexRecord, not by characters. in-flight.ts exports `fitArtifactToIndexBudget(record)`: return the record unchanged when `Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(record), "utf8") <= INDEX_BYTE_BUDGET` (defined as `MAX_FILE_BYTES - 4096` headroom; MAX_FILE_BYTES at src/cache/in-flight.ts:59, read gates verified at in-flight.ts:247 and 350); otherwise slice `record.artifact` down by the byte overshoot in a loop (each removed char removes at least 1 byte, so it converges; an `artifact.length === 0` guard covers the degenerate case), trimming a trailing lone high surrogate after each slice. This SUPERSEDES SCOPE 2's literal "size-cap the persisted artifact at MAX_FILE_BYTES" (persisting at that cap makes index.json unreadable and destroys T-024 restart rehydration). Mandated tests: escape-heavy (control-character) and multibyte artifacts serialize under budget and rehydrate. Accepted documented degradation: for pathological >~10MB artifacts, post-restart verification of findings anchored beyond the truncation point degrades to the R6 defer/flag paths; in-memory sessions keep the full artifact.

R8 (resolves round-1 codex MAJOR: reviewIntegrity identity). Ratified plan ruling 7: `ReviewIntegrityEntrySchema` carries `findingId + lensId +` the ORIGINAL per-lens claim tuple `(file, line, category)`, captured in verifyAnchors BEFORE dedup and before the survive path nulls `line`; `file` and `line` are non-nullable there (only localized findings can be flagged). The schema doc comment states the consumer contract: after dedup the corresponding `findings[]` representative may carry a different id, and two entries may map to one representative; correlate via `(file, category)` against kept findings plus `contributingLenses`, and use `lensId` for attribution. Mandated test: duplicate finding ids from two lenses produce two distinguishable integrity entries.

R9 (resolves the approve-round typecheck advisory). The `makeIndex` fixture in test/in-flight-cache.test.ts (lines 54-79 at review time; locate by content) MUST gain `artifact` and `changedFiles` fields in the same commit that extends IndexRecordSchema, or `npm run typecheck` fails (defaulted fields are required on the inferred output type) and the round-trip `toEqual` assertion breaks.

R10 (ratifies plan rulings 2, 3, 4: anchor-pass placement, scope, purity). The anchor pass runs PRE-dedup as a new first merger-pipeline stage behind an optional `anchoring` input supplied by complete.ts; existing merger unit tests that do not pass `anchoring` stay behaviorally identical. Enforcement covers localized findings only (`line !== null`); non-localized findings pass through untouched. The lens cache persists RAW pre-anchor findings (verification re-runs deterministically per round; cache hits share promptHash hence the same artifact). `hadAnyFindings` and every existing severity-count invariant are computed so the verdict.ts:86-96 coupling is preserved. `verifyAnchors` is pure. When the retained artifact is the empty string (pre-upgrade in-flight session, truncation loss; note the start param `artifact` has NO min length, src/schema/params.ts:20), the pass runs normalize-only exactly as in R1.

R11 (retention contract; T-032 hard dependency). ReviewSession gains `artifact: string` and `changedFiles: readonly string[]` (src/state/review-state.ts:52-67), threaded through `registerReview` (review-state.ts:176-220) and its sole callsite (src/tools/start.ts:234-246), and persisted in IndexRecordSchema (src/cache/in-flight.ts:99-129) through R7's budget fitter. These field NAMES and SHAPES are a cross-ticket contract: T-032 lands AFTER T-026 in this same wave and consumes the retained artifact; do not rename or reshape them. The restart acceptance test (mirror T-024 via `_clearMapOnlyForTests`, review-state.ts:595-597) stands as written.

R12 (baseline drift; re-anchor by content). The spec's VERIFIED STATE was taken at a9f49dd; T-030 has landed since (HEAD 770cfd5, suite 599/599, 9 lenses). Anchors that MOVED: the V1 denylist now sits at test/lens-bodies.test.ts:107-116 (token "evidence" at 114) with the scan loop near 179-190; the artifact label ("Diff" vs "Plan") moved to src/lenses/prompts/shared-preamble.ts:193-196; T-030 inserted a "Review method" section (~157-177) after the Tools section. The finding-format block is still shared-preamble.ts:105-127 with the line-constraint sentence at 125. The token "evidence" NO LONGER appears anywhere in shared-preamble.ts, so the spec's proof-by-existence that the denylist skips the preamble is gone; the denylist test still scans only lens BODIES via `lens.render(stage)` (test/lens-bodies.test.ts, "cross-lens structural invariants"), so the preamble remains outside its scope -- and the field MUST still be named `snippet`, never `evidence`. All other cited regions verified unchanged at 770cfd5: finding.ts:16-30 and 37-48, verdict.ts:86-96, blocking-policy.ts:62, dedup.ts:43/50/77-92, review-state.ts:52-67/176-220/595-597, in-flight.ts:59/99-129/247/350, start.ts:234-246, complete.ts:358-387.

R13 (cross-ticket edit-region coordination). T-027 (same wave) touches applyCompletion gates, buildNextActions deadline mint, lensCoverage verdict fields, and registry timeouts; T-028 rewrites the dedup collapse around dedup.ts:56-63; T-029 adds `failureScenario` to `findingObjectShape` plus its own toMerged propagation. Whichever ticket lands second inherits stale line anchors: locate EVERY edit by CONTENT anchor, and after any rebase re-verify with an explicit test that `snippet` AND `anchorRealignedFrom` (plus `failureScenario` if T-029 landed first) survive `toMerged` (dedup.ts:77-92). New verdict fields and superRefine blocks append alongside whatever T-027 added; keep all existing checks untouched.

## PLAN-REVIEW RULINGS ROUND 3 (2026-07-04, wave 3c, binding):

Adjudicated from the wave-3c round-2 plan gate that parked T-026 (verdict revise: 1 blocker with a substantive-harm memo and a required-fix memo, 1 major/security, 2 advisories). Every disputed fact re-verified at HEAD 770cfd5 (suite 599/599, tsc clean). R1-R13 stand untouched. The next plan MUST fold R-C1..R-C4 in from the start; none of these findings may be re-litigated in later plan or review rounds; reviewers and byte-review MUST treat them as spec.

R-C1 (resolves the round-2 BLOCKER "R2 VIOLATION", its SUBSTANTIVE-HARM memo, and the REQUIRED-FIX memo). PATH (a) IS ADOPTED VERBATIM; PATH (b) IS REJECTED: R2 stands unamended, there is no R14, and no plan or reviewer may self-ratify a deviation from a binding ruling (only this adjudication channel can, via the R4 mechanism). The enforcement gate in verifyAnchors is FILE-LEVEL, exactly as R2 states: any localized finding (line !== null) whose file has an entry in the diff-derived new-side index and whose quote fails the R3 window search routes per R6 (defer or survive+flag), REGARDLESS of whether the claimed line itself appears in the index. Concretely: (a) no `index.get(file).has(line)` or equivalent claimed-line-membership condition may appear in the enforcement gate; the only gate is `newSideIndex.has(file)`; (b) the absent-snippet arm is file-gated the same way: a localized finding on an in-index file with no snippet is unverified and routes per R6; (c) the plan's test A "OUTSIDE-ARTIFACT pass-through" and test E "OUTSIDE-ARTIFACT E2E" blocks are FLIPPED to assert the R6 defer/flag outcomes for in-index files with out-of-hunk claimed lines and non-matching quotes: minor lands in `deferred[]` as `evidence_unverified`; blocking at confidence >= floor survives with `line: null` plus a reviewIntegrity entry; both counts increment; (d) the DeferralReasonSchema doc comment and the anchor-module enforcement-gate documentation revert to file-gate wording, with no "claimed line in hunks" language anywhere; (e) test E's fixture constraint relaxes from "claimed line in CODE_DIFF hunks" to "file in CODE_DIFF"; (f) the out-of-scope-fence sentence justifying pass-through via round-1 finding 1 is dropped; (g) the outside-artifact REALIGN behavior is KEPT: when the claimed line is out-of-hunk but the R3 window search around it matches an in-index new-side line, realign per SCOPE 3 and count it -- this rescue path is compatible with R2/R3. Binding rationale: the motivating drift class is coordinate-system confusion (hunk-relative or old-file numbering, both named in VERIFIED STATE as legitimate lens interpretations); such claimed lines usually land outside the sparse hunk ranges, so a claimed-line gate waves through exactly the findings this ticket exists to catch and lets them die silently at the downstream consumer anchor gate. Under the file gate they surface visibly on the R6 paths. R2's mandated test (c) stands as originally written, file-gated.

R-C2 (resolves the round-2 MAJOR/security: lens-supplied server-owned fields persist into task records). ONE required design: sanitize at the submission-construction choke point in complete.ts, BEFORE applyCompletion. Verified at 770cfd5: the parse pass pushes `res.data as LensOutput` verbatim into the hoisted `submissions` array (src/tools/complete.ts:344-348), which feeds BOTH `applyCompletion` (complete.ts:396, storing into `perLensLatestOutput` via review-state.ts:500-508) AND `persistInFlightBestEffort` (complete.ts:473, writing `lensOutput: s.output` verbatim into the TaskRecord at review-state.ts:560); restart rehydration reads those records back into `perLensLatestOutput` (review-state.ts:344-357), which the merge inputs consume (complete.ts:414-421). Therefore: apply the SAME exported `sanitizeFindingForStorage` helper the plan already uses at the two lens-cache choke points (single canonical implementation, never a second stripper) to `res.data.findings` when constructing each successful submission at complete.ts:344-348. Parse-failure placeholders (complete.ts:371-383) carry no findings and need no mapping. This one callsite makes every downstream store (in-memory latest output, persisted task records, restart rehydration, merge inputs) hold sanitized findings; the anchor pass's own input strip (R1/R2) stays as defense-in-depth. REJECTED alternatives, do not revisit: sanitizing only inside persistInFlightBestEffort (leaves the in-process perLensLatestOutput contaminated for a same-process round 2), and excluding `anchorRealignedFrom` from LensFindingSchema to force a strict() reject (a lens supplying the field would then lose its ENTIRE payload to the error-placeholder path at complete.ts:358-387, and it breaks the single-shared-shape rule of finding.ts:16-20). Server-owned finding fields today = `anchorRealignedFrom` only; any future server-minted finding field MUST be added to the same helper. Mandated restart/retry test: round-1 submission whose finding carries `anchorRealignedFrom: 999` -> assert the on-disk TaskRecord JSON contains no `anchorRealignedFrom` key; `_clearMapOnlyForTests` (review-state.ts:595-597) then rehydrate -> assert the rehydrated `perLensLatestOutput` finding lacks the key; complete round 2 -> assert any `anchorRealignedFrom` on emitted findings is server-minted only.

R-C3 (resolves the round-2 ADVISORY: buildNewSideIndex empty-line extension mints phantom index entries). UPGRADED to binding, because R-C1 makes `newSideIndex.has(file)` and the per-file line set the sole enforcement inputs, so phantom entries must not exist. ONE required design: bound each hunk's new-side extension by the @@ header's declared new-side count. Parse `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` (an omitted `,d` means d = 1 per unified-diff convention); record at most d new-side lines (context " " and added "+" lines) for that hunk; once d lines are recorded the hunk is CLOSED -- subsequent blank separator lines, `diff --git` headers, `\ No newline at end of file` markers, or trailing newlines never extend it and the parser treats them as outside-hunk. The "document the approximation" fallback is REJECTED; the bound is required. Mandated test: a CODE_REVIEW diff with two files where a genuinely blank line separates file A's last hunk from file B's `diff --git` header; assert file A's index contains exactly its declared new-side lines, `has()` is false for the line one past the hunk end, and file B's index is unaffected.

R-C4 (resolves the round-2 pre-cleared ADVISORY on R10 phrasing). Both honored-in-substance judgments are RATIFIED as binding spec, R4-style; byte-review must not flag them. (a) The anchor pass ALWAYS runs, in normalize-only mode when the `anchoring` input is absent: R10's operative guarantee holds because existing merger callers stay behaviorally identical (the strip is a provable no-op for any input expressible at 770cfd5, where LensFindingSchema.strict() rejected the field, and no existing merger/dedup/tools test performs whole-object verdict equality). (b) `sanitizeFindingForStorage` at the two lens-cache choke points is REQUIRED, not a deviation: without it a lens-supplied `anchorRealignedFrom` would round-trip the cache and surface in round-2 `lens_review_start`'s `cached[]` wire array without ever passing the merger; R1 orders the field stripped from lens input and R2 orders server-owned fields stripped even on pass-through. No realignment or deferral outcome is persisted to the lens cache (R10's raw-pre-anchor persistence stands), so deterministic re-verification holds. The implementation MUST carry both justification arguments into doc comments, at the anchor-pass entry point for (a) and at the sanitizer for (b), so byte-review reads them in situ. R-C2's ingestion-point call is the third mandated callsite of the same helper.

## PLAN-REVIEW RULINGS ROUND 4 (2026-07-04, wave 3d, binding):

Adjudicated from the wave-3c round-3 plan gate that parked T-026 (final round: codex verdict revise with 3 majors and 1 minor; adversarial verdict approve with one smallest-change advisory on `anchorUnindexedFiles`, retro-ratified in R-D1). Every disputed fact re-verified at HEAD 770cfd5 (suite 599/599, tsc clean). R1-R13 and R-C1..R-C4 stand untouched. The next plan MUST fold R-D1..R-D4 in from the start; none of these findings may be re-litigated in later plan or review rounds; reviewers and byte-review MUST treat them as spec.

R-D1 (resolves the round-3 MAJOR/architecture: promptHash-binding does not attest artifact fidelity; anchorUnindexedFiles is telemetry-only). Of the reviewer's three arms, the CONTRACT-DOWNGRADE arm IS ADOPTED; the fail-closed arm and the server-digest arm are REJECTED because they contradict binding rulings or the architecture: failing closed on an empty artifact contradicts R10 verbatim (the pass runs normalize-only when the retained artifact is empty; the start param artifact has NO min length, src/schema/params.ts:20); failing closed on non-empty anchorUnindexedFiles contradicts R2 verbatim ("absence of server evidence must never brick a review" applies per-file; out-of-index findings PASS THROUGH); a server-generated trusted digest is impossible in this architecture (the server has zero repo access and never calls any API, RULES.md section 6; the artifact exists server-side only as the hop-1 caller-supplied string). ONE required design: (a) the feature contract is EXPLICITLY prompt-consistency anchoring: the server verifies lens quotes against the same caller-supplied artifact string that was embedded in every lens prompt and bound by promptHash (hashLensPrompt, src/tools/start.ts:181); it attests that all lenses and the anchor pass saw one identical artifact, and it NEVER attests that the artifact faithfully reflects any repository state; artifact authenticity remains the caller's responsibility. This trust boundary MUST appear in two doc comments: at the anchor-pass entry point (alongside the R-C4(a) justification) and on the verdict integrity fields. (b) `anchorUnindexedFiles` is upgraded from advisory telemetry to the REQUIRED verdict-level integrity surface (this retro-ratifies the wave-3c approve-round smallest-change advisory; byte-review must not flag it as scope creep): a verdict field with default empty array listing, sorted and deduplicated after R-D3 normalization, every changedFiles entry that has no entry in the diff-derived new-side index; always [] for PLAN_REVIEW and in normalize-only mode. (c) No verdict, severity, or blocking behavior changes when anchorUnindexedFiles is non-empty; a consumer that requires repo fidelity re-runs with a fresh diff (consumer obligation, escalated to the workspace; not enforceable from this repo). Mandated test: a CODE_REVIEW start whose changedFiles names a file absent from the diff completes normally; the verdict lists that file (normalized) in anchorUnindexedFiles; findings on it pass through untouched per R2.

R-D2 (resolves the round-3 MAJOR/feasibility: prompt instructs lenses to quote per Read while the index only holds diff new-side lines, so out-of-hunk findings in changed files defer or flag). The server-side semantics ARE ALREADY BINDING and win over the finding: R2 states that deferral/flagging of quotes of unchanged lines outside hunk context in a changed file "is intentional and mirrors the downstream consumer anchor gate", and R-C1 ratified the file-level gate with R6 routing precisely so coordinate-confused claimed lines surface visibly instead of dying downstream. The full-post-change-file-content arm is REJECTED: it contradicts R2 (the parsed diff new-side index is the enforcement key), requires artifact transport fenced out of this ticket (LF6 in OUT OF SCOPE), and the server has no repo access to fetch content itself. The PROMPT-ALIGNMENT arm IS ADOPTED as the one required design: (a) the preamble finding-format section gains a CODE_REVIEW-only instruction (the builder already branches on stage at the artifact label, shared-preamble.ts:193-196): for CODE_REVIEW, `line` and `snippet` may only reference post-change content shown in the Diff (added and context lines); if the defect sits in a changed file but outside the lines the Diff shows, set `line: null`, omit `snippet`, and name the exact location in `description` instead. This does not weaken the SCOPE 5 snippet mandate for localized findings, and non-localized findings pass through unverified per R10. (b) The `evidence_unverified` DeferralReason doc comment (extending R6's doc mandate, in R-C1(d) file-gate wording) states that localized findings on in-index files whose quotes are not present in the diff new-side are treated as unverified BY DESIGN. (c) The R-C1(g) rescue stands: an out-of-hunk claimed line whose R3 window search matches an in-index new-side line is realigned and counted, not deferred. Mandated tests: the pinned preamble test asserts the new CODE_REVIEW sentence verbatim AND asserts it is absent from the PLAN_REVIEW rendering; R2's mandated tests and R-C1(c)'s flipped tests stand unchanged.

R-D3 (resolves the round-3 MAJOR/edge cases: exact string path matching misclassifies backslash, dot-slash-prefixed, and rename/copy paths). ADOPTED as specified. ONE required design: a single exported helper `normalizeRepoPath(p: string): string` in the anchor module: convert every backslash to a forward slash, then strip leading "./" segments repeatedly, then collapse consecutive slashes to one. No case folding, no ".." resolution, no trailing-slash handling; it is a comparison key, never a rewrite. Applied at EXACTLY three comparison points: (1) the diff parser stores each new-side index key as normalizeRepoPath of the path taken from the "+++ b/<path>" header with the "b/" prefix stripped ("+++ /dev/null" never creates an entry; a pure rename with no content hunks contributes no new-side lines, so that file has no index entry and findings on it pass through per R2, which is correct because there is nothing to verify); (2) changedFiles entries are normalized, then deduplicated, only when computing anchorUnindexedFiles; (3) finding.file is normalized for the newSideIndex.has() gate and the per-file line lookups. Emitted findings keep their original `file` string byte-for-byte (dedup keys at src/merger/dedup.ts:50 are untouched; the pre-existing dot-slash alias non-dedup is out of scope); persisted ReviewSession/IndexRecord values stay exactly as supplied (R11 field shapes untouched; normalize at use, never at storage). registry.ts's activation-side `normalize` (src/lenses/registry.ts:208-209, backslash-only) stays untouched: changing activation behavior is out of ticket scope; the anchor module doc comment cross-references it as the activation-side variant. Mandated tests: (a) a changedFiles entry with backslashes whose forward-slash form the diff indexes is NOT listed in anchorUnindexedFiles; (b) a finding with file "./src/x.ts" gates against the "src/x.ts" index entry (enforced: realigned or routed per R6, not passed through); (c) two changedFiles entries normalizing to the same missing path produce one anchorUnindexedFiles entry; (d) a rename-with-hunks diff indexes under the new-side path, and a finding on the OLD path passes through per R2; (e) a deletion ("+++ /dev/null") creates no index entry and a finding on the deleted file passes through per R2.

R-D4 (resolves the round-3 MINOR/observability: reviewIntegrity entries correlate to kept findings only via (file, category), which is ambiguous when multiple flagged findings share both). The reviewer's second arm (pin the kept finding id to the original findingId and enforce it in schema) is REJECTED: it contradicts R8's ratified consumer contract ("after dedup the corresponding findings[] representative may carry a different id, and two entries may map to one representative"), and cross-lens duplicate ids (R8's own mandated test) make findingId non-unique as a key. The SERVER-MINTED CORRELATION ID arm IS ADOPTED as the one required design, additive to R8 (R8 stands unamended): (a) findingObjectShape gains `integrityKey: z.string().min(1).optional()` (single shared shape per finding.ts:16-20; both schemas stay .strict()). (b) The field is SERVER-OWNED: it joins `anchorRealignedFrom` in the single `sanitizeFindingForStorage` strip list (R-C2's clause that any future server-minted finding field MUST be added to the same helper applies), so lens-supplied values are stripped at all three mandated callsites; only verifyAnchors mints it. (c) Minting: at flag time in verifyAnchors, "ie-<n>" with n the 1-based flag order within the pass (deterministic per completion round), set on BOTH the surviving flagged finding and its ReviewIntegrityEntry, whose schema gains a REQUIRED `integrityKey: z.string().min(1)` (the entry schema is new in this ticket, so no back-compat concern; R8's findingId, lensId, and original claim tuple stand unchanged). (d) Dedup MUST NOT collapse a finding carrying integrityKey into another finding, nor another finding into it (this pins the plan's existing non-collapse of flagged findings as spec), guaranteeing 1:1 entry-to-kept-finding correlation; `toMerged` propagates integrityKey, and R13's survive-toMerged test extends to cover it alongside snippet and anchorRealignedFrom. (e) The R8 doc comment is SUPPLEMENTED, not amended: integrityKey is the primary correlation key; (file, category) plus contributingLenses remains documented as the fallback for readers of pre-upgrade cached verdicts. (f) Verdict superRefine (appended alongside the R4/ACCEPTANCE-4 count checks, existing checks untouched per R13): every reviewIntegrity entry's integrityKey matches exactly one findings[] member, and no two findings[] members share an integrityKey; sound because R6 guarantees an integrity-flagged finding's representative is never floor-deferred. Mandated test: two flagged findings sharing (file, category) from different lenses yield two integrity entries with distinct integrityKeys, each resolving to exactly one distinct findings[] member.
